name: Edward P. Cattell
bio: Farm hand at Kirkwood, New Jersey, and a friend of the Stafford family, whom Whitman met in May 1876 and met again by Timber Creek and by the pond on moonlight nights through the following year. Whitman noted his age as 'about 25 or 6' in 1876, which is as close to a birth year as the record comes; his people lived at Gloucester, and his grandfather or great-grandfather Jonas Cattell was a Revolutionary soldier and celebrated runner, whom Whitman thought interesting enough to write up in the Philadelphia Times in 1879. In January 1877 Whitman wrote asking him to stop calling at the Stafford farm and to tell nobody, while assuring him of 'unalterable love'. Cattell wrote back that October, in his own spelling, that he loved him and always would. **No dates of birth or death are recorded for him anywhere consulted** - the paper thins exactly where the money does, and he is on this map for the same reason the unnamed men of Wilde's exile are.
